summary.implementedScope: Replaced the fake immediate-refresh success path with a runtime-backed hydration executor that resolves a real process working-copy target, uses the provider adapter hydration/rehydration seam, returns pending/failed/not-available truthfully, and only marks a source hydrated after actual runtime refresh completion.
summary.acceptanceRationale: Story-lead is pausing for caller ruling 03-hydration-and-freshness-management-story-run-001-ruling-018 before impl-lead can accept the story.

evidence: The story/design says project-scoped actions appear in the project source section and Story 3 includes refresh/rehydration for `stale` and `not_hydrated` attachments. In the client, `renderSourceAttachmentSection()` renders refresh controls for any source whose hydration state is `stale` or `not_hydrated` regardless of scope (`apps/platform/client/features/projects/source-attachment-section.ts`). In the new runtime path, `RuntimeSourceHydrationExecutor.resolveTargetProcessId()` returns `null` for project-scoped attachments unless exactly one current process references the source, and `refreshRecoverableSource()` then returns `kind: 'not_available'` with message `no single current process working copy owns this source attachment` (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-refresh.service.ts`). The modified API tests only verify successful refresh for process-scoped attachments; no server or client test proves the project-scoped case or suppresses the project-shell control when the backend will 409. This leaves project-scoped recoverability behavior unresolved and can present a false recovery path on the project shell.

rulingRequest.question: For project-scoped source attachments shown in the project shell, what should refresh do when the attachment is stale or not_hydrated but there is no single unambiguous current process working-copy target?
rulingRequest.defaultRecommendation: Hide or disable the project-shell refresh control unless the backend can identify exactly one current process working-copy target; keep refresh enabled for process-scoped rows and for project-scoped rows with one unambiguous owning process. This avoids falsely promising recovery and aligns with AC-3.2 until a later story defines cross-process/project-level hydration semantics.
evidence: Verifier finding story-3-project-scope-refresh-target-ambiguity is blocking and affects AC-3.2, AC-3.3, TC-3.2a, TC-3.2c, and TC-3.3a.
Client project source section renders refresh controls for any stale or not_hydrated source regardless of scope.
RuntimeSourceHydrationExecutor returns SOURCE_ATTACHMENT_REFRESH_NOT_AVAILABLE for project-scoped attachments unless exactly one current process references the source.
